title: 35 per hour annual salary: what you earn, tax and super explained
description: Calculate your 35 per hour annual salary for a 38-hour week. See fortnightly pay, tax, Medicare levy and super guarantee with our Australian guide.
salarySummary: At $35 per hour for a standard 38-hour week, your annual salary is $69,160 before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from $35 per hour?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52. For a full‑time employee working 38 hours per week: $35 × 38 = $1,330 per week, and $1,330 × 52 = $69,160 per year. This is the standard formula used by the Fair Work Ombudsman and the Australian Bureau of Statistics. If you work fewer or more hours, adjust the weekly figure accordingly.

faqs.q: What tax and Medicare levy will I pay on a $35 per hour annual salary?
faqs.a: On $69,160 in 2026–27, you pay no tax on the first $18,200, then 15% on the next $26,800 ($4,020), and 30% on the remaining $24,160 ($7,248). Total tax is $11,268. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income, which is $1,383. Combined deductions are $12,651, leaving an estimated take‑home pay of $56,509 per year. These figures use the resident tax rates and the standard Medicare levy; your actual amount may differ if you have dependants or a Medicare levy reduction.

faqs.q: Does the $35 per hour rate include casual loading or super?
faqs.a: No. The $35 rate is your base hourly rate. If you are a casual employee, the Fair Work Commission’s casual loading of 25% is added on top, making your casual rate $43.75 per hour. Superannuation guarantee of 12% is paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings, so for a $69,160 annual salary the employer contributes an extra $8,299. The [timesheet](/topics/casual-loading) has a checkbox to add casual loading – never type a rate that already includes loading. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional contribution.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding your 35 per hour annual salary

If you earn **$35 per hour** and work a standard full‑time week of 38 hours, your **35 per hour annual salary** is $69,160. This figure comes from the simple formula: hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks. It is the same method used by the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) guide and the Australian Bureau of Statistics for its average weekly earnings estimates.

### The weekly and fortnightly breakdown

Your weekly pay at $35 per hour for 38 hours is $1,330. Multiply that by two to get your fortnightly pay: $2,660. Knowing your fortnightly amount can help with budgeting and comparing to salary offers that are quoted per fortnight. The [reference tables](/data) show that $35 per hour is well above the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026) and above many award rates.

### Tax and Medicare on $69,160

Using the 2026–27 resident tax rates, your annual tax on $69,160 is $11,268. The Medicare levy adds a further 2% ($1,383), bringing total deductions to $12,651. Your estimated take‑home pay is therefore $56,509 per year, or about $1,087 per week. The [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page explains how the tax‑free threshold and marginal rates apply. Note that the Medicare levy reduction thresholds used here are the 2025–26 single figures because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this guide.

### Superannuation is paid on top

Your employer must pay super guarantee of 12% on your ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a $69,160 annual salary, that means an extra $8,299 contributed to your super fund. This is not deducted from your pay – it is an additional cost to your employer. The [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) article covers how salary sacrifice and contribution caps work.

### Casual loading and award rates

If you are a casual employee, you are entitled to a 25% loading on your base rate. For a $35 per hour base rate, the casual rate becomes $43.75 per hour. The [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains that the loading compensates for the lack of paid leave. When using the [timesheet](/), never enter a rate that already includes casual loading – instead, check the casual loading box and the calculator will add the 25% on top. Award rates set by the Fair Work Commission may also apply to your industry; they can be higher or lower than $35 per hour. The [pay guides](/blog) list common award classifications.

### Comparing $35 per hour to averages

According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, full‑time adult ordinary time earnings averaged $2,083.70 per week in May 2026. That equates to about $54.83 per hour for a 38‑hour week. Your $35 per hour is below that average, but it is above the all‑employees total average of $1,579.20 per week ($41.56 per hour), which includes part‑time workers. Remember that these are averages, not medians, and your specific job may have a different typical rate. The [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page has more detail.

### Important assumptions and limitations

The annual salary shown here assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. It also assumes you are a resident for tax purposes and claim the full tax‑free threshold. If you have a HELP debt, a Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging arrangements, your take‑home pay will differ. The [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page outlines the legal minimums, and the [job pay](/topics/job-pay) page helps you find industry‑specific rates.

### Using the timesheet calculator

To see your own figures, visit the [timesheet](/). Enter your base hourly rate – for example, $35 – and select your hours per week. If you are casual, tick the casual loading checkbox. The calculator will show your weekly, fortnightly, and annual pay, along with estimated tax, Medicare, and super. Remember that the super amount is an estimate based on 12% of ordinary earnings and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. The tax estimate uses the 2026–27 resident scale and the standard Medicare levy. Always check with the Australian Taxation Office or a qualified adviser for your personal situation.
